candidates.name: Guggenheim Museum
candidates.price: Adults €18.00; +65, students, -26: €8; -18 free (online prices, door prices €1-2 higher)
candidates.hours: Tue-Sun 10:00 to 20:00; Jul and Aug: daily 10:00 to 20:00. Closed Jan 1 and Dec 25
candidates.content: Frank Gehry's spectacular twisting titanium-clad modern art museum is perhaps the most celebrated building of the 1990s, even starting what would be called the 'Bilbao-effect': The idea in urban planning that a star-quality buildi

candidates.name: Museo de Bellas Artes
candidates.price: For 2025 until major renovation works are complete: free
candidates.hours: Mon Wed-Sat 10:00-20:00; Sun and public holidays 10:00-15:00; Tue closed. 1 Jan and 25 December: closed
candidates.content: The Museum of Fine Art's remarkable collection boasts more than 6,000 works dating from the 12th century to the present day, and includes paintings, sculptures, drawings, engravings and decorative objects. From 2023 the museum is

candidates.name: Basque Museum
candidates.price: Adults: €3.5; +65 12-26 and groups €2. Children under 12 & everyone on Th: free
candidates.hours: Mon Wed-Fri 10:00-19:00; Sat 10-13:30,16:00-19:00; Sun 11:00-14:00. Tue and public holidays: closed
candidates.content: Established in 1921 to focus on the prehistory, archaeology, ethnography and history of Euskadi (Basque homeland). Not a particularly well laid out museum. It will be of passing interest to people who study Basque culture.

candidates.name: Itsasmuseum
candidates.hours: Winter: Tue-Fri 10:00-14:00, 16:00-18:00; Sat Sun 10:00-14:00 and 16:00-20:00; summer: call to check
candidates.content: It's in what used to be the Euskalduna shipyard, this maritime museum is next to the current Euskalduna Performing Arts Centre. The museum covers an area of 27,000 m², 7,000 m² for indoor exhibitions and 20,000 m² for outdoor exhi

candidates.name: Museo Taurino (Bullfighting Museum)
candidates.content: Martín Agüero, 1, Plaza de Toros de Vista Alegre, (Near Plaza Zabalburu). Next to a bullring, the Museo Taurino highlights the role bullfighting has played in Euskadi.

candidates.name: Puppy
candidates.content: Not a museum, but it is directly in the front of the Guggenheim Museum, created by Jeff Koons. It's one of the most famous symbols of modern Bilbao. It is a west Highland terrier 12 m high covered in flowers that are changed each

candidates.name: Museo Diocesano de Arte Sacro (Museum of Sacred Art)
candidates.price: General €3; student, senior, and under 18 €1.5; free on Tuesdays
candidates.content: A former convent founded in 1515 by Dominican nuns.

candidates.name: Cathedral of St. James (Santiago)
candidates.content: Gothic-style 14th-century cathedral, named after Bilbao's official patron saint. Three naves and small Gothic cloisters. The building was designated a cathedral in 1949. Its neo-Gothic tower and main façade were designed by Severi

candidates.name: Iglesia de San Antón
candidates.content: Gothic style church from the first half of the 15th century (1422). Dedicated to San Anton in the 16th century, the building is a mixture of styles including a renaissance portico and baroque tower which was built in 1777. The chu

candidates.name: Basílica de Begoña
candidates.content: Overlooking Bilbao, this is perhaps the most symbolic religious building in the city. Built in the 16th-century by Sancho Martinez de Arego, who was also responsible for the Iglesia San Anton. It is a basilica of three naves. Duri

candidates.name: Iglesia de San Nicolás
candidates.content: The Iglesia de San Nicolás, finished in the 19th century, is dedicated to the patron saint of sailors. One of the best examples of Baroque architecture in Vizcaya.

candidates.name: Mercado de la Ribera
candidates.content: Another emblem next to the Iglesia de San Antón is the Mercado de la Rivera. One of the biggest covered markets in Europe. It was built in 1929 on the site of the original Rivera Street market. Produce fish and meat are sold in th

candidates.name: Plaza Nueva
candidates.content: Bilbao's Plaza Nueva was first named Plaza de Fernando VII. Construction began on the plaza on December 31, 1829 and finished exactly 20 years later on December 31, 1849. This plaza was the seat of the Diputación de Vizcaya until

candidates.name: Palacio de la Diputación
candidates.content: Ornately decorated palace situated on the Grand Vía. Baroque-style monument designed by Luis Aladrén in 1897 to serve as the seat of the Diputación Foral de Bizkaia (Vizcaya) and inaugurated on July 31, 1900. The interior is just

candidates.name: Museo de Reproducciones Artísticas (Museum of Artistic Reproductions)
candidates.content: Full-scale reproductions of the world's most famous works of art. Call ahead for a guided visit.

candidates.name: Vizcaya Bridge
candidates.content: Also known as Puente Colgante (the hanging bridge), this is the only UNESCO World Heritage site in Spain listed in the "Industrial" category. You can use your Barik card to cross but the price is the same as buying a ticket.

candidates.name: Azkuna Zentroa
candidates.content: An amazing building which has been modernized (according to designs by Philippe Starck and Thibaut Mathieu). It is an amazing complex containing a library, several bars and restaurants, a cinema and even a roof swimming pool with

candidates.name: Teatro Arriaga
candidates.content: Inaugurated on 31 May 1890, on the site of several former theatres, the first Teatro Arriaga burnt down on 22 December 1914. The second Teatro Arriaga opened on 5 June 1919. Evocative of the Opera House in Paris, the theater has a

candidates.name: La Concordia Station
candidates.content: It was built between 1898-1902 on the banks of the Nervión. Designed by the engineer Valentín Gorbeña, with the art nouveau main façade added later with a design by the architect Severino Achúcarro.

candidates.name: Palacio Euskalduna
candidates.alt: Euskalduna Conference Center and Concert Hall
candidates.content: A convention centre and concert hall housed in a modern building at the far end of paseo Uribitarte. Home to the Bilbao Symphony Orchestra and Bilbao Opera.

candidates.name: Plaza Elíptica and Gran Vía
candidates.content: On the stretch of the Gran Vía between Plaza Abando and Plaza Elíptica is the main shopping and fashion district of Bilbao. On this short stretch you can find tons of clothes shops (For, Zara, Mango, H&M) and department store El C

candidates.name: Parque Etxebarria
candidates.content: The site of a former steel factory, this park was created in the 1980s as the first step of reorienting Bilbao from the industrial sector to the service sector. Wonderful views of the Casco Viejo and the Teatro Arriaga. There is a

candidates.name: Ayuntamiento (City Hall)
candidates.content: Also known as la Casa Consistorial or Udaletxea. The city hall opened in 1892. Designed by architect Jaquin Rucoba in neo-baroque style. Don't miss the main reception area, called Arab Salon.

candidates.name: Zubizuri
candidates.content: The graceful white pedestrian bridge designed by Santiago Calatrava, actually zubi zuri means white bridge in Basque. It spans the Nervión connecting the riverwalks Campo Volatin and Mazarredo. Be careful: the bridge is slippery w

candidates.name: Biblioteca Municipal de Bidebarrieta
candidates.content: Commissioned by El Sitio society at the end of the 19th century, this building was built by architect Severino de Achucarro as a social hall. Now home to the city's historical archives and library.

candidates.name: Palacio de Ibaigane
candidates.content: Home to the Athletic Club de Bilbao, Bilbao's football team. Built in the early 20th century. Note the arched entranceway. The nearest metro stop is Moyúa.

candidates.name: Palacio de Olábarri
candidates.alt: Palacete del Puerto Autónomo de Bilbao
candidates.content: An interesting mix of several architectural styles. In the late 19th century it was the residence of Bilbaino entrepreneur José María de Olábarri. Now the seat of Bilbao's port authority.

candidates.name: Estación Abando
candidates.content: Even if you are not going to take a train, visit the platforms, there is an impressive stained glass atrium depicting some traditional Basque jobs.

candidates.name: Bar Jamon Jamon
candidates.content: Simple neighbourhood bar. Good ham baguettes (bocadillo). Freshly baked baguettes, counter-carved Spanish Ham and the friendly service of Luis and Nekane. Not fancy but familiar with authentic atmosphere.

candidates.name: Kafe Antzokia
candidates.content: This former theatre was converted into a multi-purpose venue in 1995. It is best known for promoting the Basque culture, both as an artists' venue and for the clientele. With a varied schedule of concerts of Basque and internation

candidates.name: Basquery
candidates.content: Brewpub with eight of their beers on tap. Bistro with view of brewery with pizzas, burgers, salads and other dishes. Vegan and vegetarian dishes are also available.

candidates.name: Dakar
candidates.content: Nightly karaoke and Spanish dance music.

candidates.name: Gran Casino Nervión
candidates.content: Two bars, on-site restaurant. Formal/semi-formal dress required.

candidates.name: Panko
candidates.content: Great stylish place that sells bread, pinxtos and meals. Good selection of regional wines

candidates.name: Singular
candidates.content: Good choice of beers with at least one local one on draught. Additional choices in cans. Good selection of Raciones if you want a snack.

candidates.name: Cafe Iruña
candidates.content: With its Arabesque motifs and antique mouldings it is a sight to behold. If you go at night, you can also get some nice shikabobs - some of the only ones you'll find in Bilbao.

candidates.name: Cafe Nervión
candidates.content: Wonderful views of the river.

candidates.name: Lamiak
candidates.content: Comfortable coffee house, with chocolate cake to die for.

candidates.name: Galeon
candidates.content: Maritime motif a mermaid statue at the entrance and decoration resembling the inside of a ship.

candidates.name: Aritz
candidates.content: Was once one of the best Pintxos bars in Bilbao, quite out of the way (almost hidden really in a very small, one way street away from the main thoroughfares). Ask for it and you will be given directions. It is worth the walk since

candidates.name: à table
candidates.content: Cozy place in the old quarter of Bilbao. An authentic Basque-French restaurant offering a true flavour of that traditional cuisine. Good cellar. Reservation required. Service in English.

candidates.name: Zortziko
candidates.content: Traditional Basque dishes such as pigeon breast or marinated sea bass. Formal environment with late Victorian style furnishing, frequently booked days in advance. Ask about reservations to dine in the wine cellar.

candidates.name: Restaurante Kasko
candidates.content: This restaurant claims that their Pintxos are a miniaturization of Basque cooking culture. The Pintxos are presented very nicely and in an appetizing way on the bar counter. Staff proficient in English, occasionally live Piano mus

candidates.name: Malatesta
candidates.hours: From 11:00 to 22:30, Fri and Sat until 02:00. Mon closed for rest
candidates.content: A place where you can have a drink, snack on pinchos and eat in the heart of Bilbao's Siete Calles. Vegetarian and vegan options. There is always an exhibition on, and cultural events are held here.

december.text: Birthplace of Miguel Unamuno: Spanish author born on 29 September 1864. His works include the novels Niebla and San Manuel Bueno, Martir, which are both read in AP Spanish Literature classes in the United States. Unamuno died on 31 December 1936 in Salamanca.
